conflicts.fact: Whether rotation produces direct or opposite congruence (and whether rotation reverses orientation)
conflicts.versions: Lesson 7 teaches that rotation gives OPPOSITE congruence (needs lifting, cyclic vertex order reverses, clockwise becomes anticlockwise), grouped with reflection. Lesson 8 states the object and image are always DIRECTLY congruent (same orientation type). Lessons 2-4 present rotation as a turn that preserves shape, size and orientation, with no mention of reversal. Lesson 7 contradicts the standard result and Lesson 8.

conflicts.fact: Direction of the 12:15 rotation of the minute hand (angle and direction of 12:15, 12:45 positions)
conflicts.versions: Lessons 1, 3 and 8 treat the hand as moving 90° clockwise at 12:15, 180° at 12:30, and 270° clockwise at 12:45. Lesson 4 maps (0,5) to (-5,0) after 90° anticlockwise as the 12:15 position, (0,-5) at 12:30, and (5,0) after 270° anticlockwise at 12:45; this contradicts the clockwise motion of the clock. Lesson 3's Predict phase also has the hand sweeping 90° anticlockwise from 12 to 9, and calls 12:45 'also 90° anticlockwise'.

conflicts.fact: Number of clock positions in the anchoring phenomenon
conflicts.versions: Lessons 1-7 and the phenomenon use four positions (12:00, 12:15, 12:30, 12:45). Lesson 8's Observed section lists five (adding 1:00) while saying 'all four positions', and the Explain activity uses 1:00 as a fourth rotation.
Lesson 6 says the full 12-mark clock face has order-12 rotational symmetry with 30° angle. Lesson 8 says the circular clock face has infinite rotational symmetry.

conflicts.fact: Minute-hand angle used in Lesson 5 predict phase
conflicts.versions: Lesson 5 shows the minute hand moving from 12 to 4, i.e. 120° clockwise, which is not a position in the 15-minute-interval anchoring phenomenon (12:00, 12:15, 12:30, 12:45). The phenomenon states that the hand moves in 90° steps.

conflicts.fact: Lesson numbering of earlier activities and clock hand used
conflicts.versions: Lesson 7 says translation images came from Lesson 3, rotation from Lesson 4, and reflection from 'Lesson 2 sub-strand revision', whereas Lessons 2-5 are all rotation lessons and no translation or reflection pairs were produced. Lesson 7 also uses the hour hand at 3:00 and 9:00 in its overview, while the phenomenon and the Predict phase use the minute hand.
